requirements.quote:
In its Adj-RIBs-In, a BGP speaker may have several routes to the same
   destination that have the same degree of preference.  The local
   speaker can select only one of these routes for inclusion in the
   associated Loc-RIB.  The local speaker considers all routes with the
   same degrees of preference, both those received from internal peers,
   and those received from external peers.
requirements.condition: Several Adj-RIBs-In routes to the same destination have the same degree of preference.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Select more than one of these routes for inclusion in the associated Loc-RIB.
requirements.why_checkable: The Loc-RIB winner count for equally preferred alternatives can be checked.

requirements.quote:
In its Adj-RIBs-In, a BGP speaker may have several routes to the same
   destination that have the same degree of preference.  The local
   speaker can select only one of these routes for inclusion in the
   associated Loc-RIB.  The local speaker considers all routes with the

requirements.condition: Breaking a tie between routes to the same destination with the same degree of preference.
requirements.required_behavior: Consider all such routes from both internal and external peers.
requirements.why_checkable: Candidate construction can be checked with equally preferred IBGP and EBGP routes.

requirements.quote:
The tie-breaking algorithm begins by considering all equally
   preferable routes to the same destination, and then selects routes to
   be removed from consideration.  The algorithm terminates as soon as
   only one route remains in consideration.  The criteria MUST be
   applied in the order specified.
requirements.condition: Starting the Phase 2 tie-breaking algorithm.
requirements.required_behavior: Begin with all equally preferable routes to the same destination and progressively remove candidates.
requirements.why_checkable: Initial candidate membership and subsequent elimination can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
The tie-breaking algorithm begins by considering all equally

requirements.condition: Only one route remains in consideration during tie breaking.
requirements.required_behavior: Terminate the tie-breaking algorithm as soon as one route remains.
requirements.why_checkable: Termination can be checked after each elimination criterion.

requirements.quote:
The tie-breaking algorithm begins by considering all equally
   preferable routes to the same destination, and then selects routes to
   be removed from consideration.  The algorithm terminates as soon as
   only one route remains in consideration.  The criteria MUST be
   applied in the order specified.
requirements.condition: Applying Phase 2 tie-breaking criteria.
requirements.required_behavior: MUST apply the criteria in their specified order: AS_PATH count, Origin, MULTI_EXIT_DISC, EBGP over IBGP, then interior cost for the criteria shown in this chunk.
requirements.why_checkable: The comparison sequence and behavior when earlier criteria decide the winner can be checked.

requirements.quote:
Several of the criteria are described using pseudo-code.  Note that
   the pseudo-code shown was chosen for clarity, not efficiency.  It is
   not intended to specify any particular implementation.  BGP
   implementations MAY use any algorithm that produces the same results
   as those described here.
requirements.condition: Implementing the specified tie-breaking procedure.
requirements.required_behavior: MAY use any algorithm that produces the same results as the described procedure.
requirements.why_checkable: An alternative implementation can be checked for outcome equivalence to the specified criteria.

requirements.quote:
a) Remove from consideration all routes that are not tied for
         having the smallest number of AS numbers present in their
         AS_PATH attributes.  Note that when counting this number, an
         AS_SET counts as 1, no matter how many ASes are in the set.
requirements.condition: Applying the first tie-breaking criterion to equally preferable routes to the same destination.
requirements.required_behavior: Remove every route not tied for the smallest number of AS numbers in its AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.why_checkable: Route sets with different AS_PATH counts give a deterministic surviving subset.

requirements.quote:
a) Remove from consideration all routes that are not tied for
         having the smallest number of AS numbers present in their
         AS_PATH attributes.  Note that when counting this number, an
         AS_SET counts as 1, no matter how many ASes are in the set.
requirements.condition: Counting AS numbers in AS_PATH for tie-breaking criterion (a).
requirements.required_behavior: Count each AS_SET as one regardless of how many ASes the set contains.
requirements.why_checkable: AS_PATH counting can be checked with AS_SET segments of differing cardinalities.

requirements.quote:
b) Remove from consideration all routes that are not tied for
         having the lowest Origin number in their Origin attribute.
requirements.condition: More than one candidate remains after criterion (a); applying criterion (b).
requirements.required_behavior: Remove every route not tied for the lowest Origin number in its Origin attribute.
requirements.why_checkable: Origin comparisons on routes tied at the earlier step determine the survivor set.

requirements.quote:
c) Remove from consideration routes with less-preferred
         MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes.  MULTI_EXIT_DISC is only comparable
         between routes learned from the same neighboring AS (the
         neighboring AS is determined from the AS_PATH attribute).
         Routes that do not have the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute are
         considered to have the lowest possible MULTI_EXIT_DISC value.
requirements.condition: More than one candidate remains after AS_PATH and Origin criteria; applying criterion (c).
requirements.required_behavior: Remove routes with less-preferred MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes when comparing routes learned from the same neighboring AS.
requirements.why_checkable: Candidate sets sharing a neighboring AS and differing in MED expose the elimination rule.

requirements.quote:
for m = all routes still under consideration
           for n = all routes still under consideration
               if (neighborAS(m) == neighborAS(n)) and (MED(n) < MED(m))
                   remove route m from consideration
requirements.condition: At criterion (c), two routes still under consideration have the same neighboring AS and MED(n) is less than MED(m).
requirements.required_behavior: Remove route m from consideration.
requirements.why_checkable: Numeric MED ordering and equal-neighbor predicate can be directly checked.

requirements.quote:
c) Remove from consideration routes with less-preferred
         MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes.  MULTI_EXIT_DISC is only comparable
         between routes learned from the same neighboring AS (the
         neighboring AS is determined from the AS_PATH attribute).
         Routes that do not have the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute are
         considered to have the lowest possible MULTI_EXIT_DISC value.
requirements.condition: Applying MULTI_EXIT_DISC comparisons at criterion (c).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Compare MULTI_EXIT_DISC values between routes learned from different neighboring ASes.
requirements.why_checkable: Different-neighbor routes can be checked to ensure MED does not eliminate either route.

requirements.quote:
c) Remove from consideration routes with less-preferred
         MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes.  MULTI_EXIT_DISC is only comparable
         between routes learned from the same neighboring AS (the
         neighboring AS is determined from the AS_PATH attribute).
         Routes that do not have the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute are
         considered to have the lowest possible MULTI_EXIT_DISC value.
requirements.condition: Determining the neighboring AS for the MULTI_EXIT_DISC criterion.
requirements.required_behavior: Determine the neighboring AS from the AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.why_checkable: The neighbor-AS derivation can be inspected against the route AS_PATH.

requirements.quote:
In the pseudo-code above, MED(n) is a function that returns the
         value of route n's MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute.  If route n has
         no MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute, the function returns the lowest
         possible MULTI_EXIT_DISC value (i.e., 0).
requirements.condition: A candidate route has no MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the lowest possible MULTI_EXIT_DISC value, zero, for MED comparison.
requirements.why_checkable: Missing MED can be compared against explicit zero and positive MED values.

requirements.quote:
Similarly, neighborAS(n) is a function that returns the
         neighbor AS from which the route was received.  If the route is
         learned via IBGP, and the other IBGP speaker didn't originate
         the route, it is the neighbor AS from which the other IBGP
         speaker learned the route.  If the route is learned via IBGP,
         and the other IBGP speaker either (a) originated the route, or
         (b) created the route by aggregation and the AS_PATH attribute
         of the aggregate route is either empty or begins with an
         AS_SET, it is the local AS.
requirements.condition: Determining neighborAS for a route received from an external neighbor.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the neighbor AS from which the route was received.
requirements.why_checkable: External neighbor identity can be compared with the neighborAS comparison key.

requirements.quote:

requirements.condition: A route is learned via IBGP and the other IBGP speaker did not originate it, except the explicitly described local-AS aggregation case.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the neighbor AS from which the other IBGP speaker learned the route as neighborAS.
requirements.why_checkable: An IBGP-learned external route can be checked for its original neighboring-AS comparison key.

requirements.required_behavior: Use the local AS as neighborAS.
requirements.why_checkable: Locally originated IBGP routes have an observable local-AS comparison key.

used in the comparison with IBGP-learned routes.  For IBGP-

requirements.quote:
d) If at least one of the candidate routes was received via EBGP,
         remove from consideration all routes that were received via
         IBGP.
requirements.condition: After criteria (a), (b), and (c), multiple candidates remain and at least one was received via EBGP.
requirements.required_behavior: At criterion (d), remove every candidate received via IBGP.
requirements.why_checkable: Mixed IBGP and EBGP candidate sets tied at earlier criteria have a defined surviving provenance.

requirements.quote:
e) Remove from consideration any routes with less-preferred
         interior cost.  The interior cost of a route is determined by
         calculating the metric to the NEXT_HOP for the route using the
         Routing Table.  If the NEXT_HOP hop for a route is reachable,
         but no cost can be determined, then this step should be skipped
         (equivalently, consider all routes to have equal costs).
requirements.condition: Multiple candidates remain after criterion (d), and interior-cost comparison is applicable.
requirements.required_behavior: At criterion (e), remove routes with less-preferred interior cost.
requirements.why_checkable: Candidates tied at preceding criteria can be checked for minimum-interior-cost survival.

requirements.quote:
e) Remove from consideration any routes with less-preferred
         interior cost.  The interior cost of a route is determined by
         calculating the metric to the NEXT_HOP for the route using the
         Routing Table.  If the NEXT_HOP hop for a route is reachable,
         but no cost can be determined, then this step should be skipped
         (equivalently, consider all routes to have equal costs).
requirements.condition: Determining a route interior cost for criterion (e).
requirements.required_behavior: Calculate the metric to that route NEXT_HOP using the Routing Table.
requirements.why_checkable: The comparison metric can be traced to the Routing Table entry for NEXT_HOP.

requirements.quote:
e) Remove from consideration any routes with less-preferred
         interior cost.  The interior cost of a route is determined by
         calculating the metric to the NEXT_HOP for the route using the
         Routing Table.  If the NEXT_HOP hop for a route is reachable,
         but no cost can be determined, then this step should be skipped
         (equivalently, consider all routes to have equal costs).
requirements.condition: At criterion (e), a route NEXT_HOP is reachable but no cost can be determined.
requirements.required_behavior: This step should be skipped, equivalently treating all routes as having equal costs.
requirements.why_checkable: A reachable route lacking a determined cost can be checked for bypass of interior-cost elimination.
